title: Nursing home regulation after Windsor Convalescent Home lapses
asked: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked whether there are plans to strengthen nursing home regulation to prevent systemic lapses like those at Windsor Convalescent Home, and if not, why not.
response: MOH says it already conducts regular audits, thematic reviews, inspections and off-cycle audits of nursing homes, and escalates when serious repeated gaps are not fixed. It revoked the licences of Windsor Convalescent Home and LC Nursing Home after remediation was inadequate, arranging for Vanguard Healthcare to step in. It will share recent audit findings and manpower training and grant support with the sector, and says it cannot coordinate private claims because care is a contract between the resident and the nursing home.

key_points.point: MOH conducts regular and periodic audits, special thematic reviews and inspections on nursing homes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we conduct regular and periodic audits, special thematic reviews and inspections on nursing homes

key_points.point: If gaps are serious, repeated and not seriously rectified, MOH escalates measures, as with Windsor Convalescent Home and LC Nursing Home.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: if the gaps are serious, repeated and there is a lack of serious effort to rectify them, such as in the case of Windsor Convalescent Home and LC Nursing Home, MOH will have to escalate our measures

key_points.point: When remediation was inadequate or not sustained for the two operators, MOH revoked their licences and arranged for Vanguard Healthcare to step in.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: When we ascertained that the remediation efforts were inadequate or were not sustained for the two operators, we revoked their licences and arranged for Vanguard Healthcare to step in

key_points.point: MOH and the Agency for Integrated Care will share recent audit findings and manpower training and grant support with the nursing home sector.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: MOH and the Agency for Integrated Care will also be sharing the findings of our recent audits, and the various manpower training and grant support available with the nursing home sector

key_points.point: MOH cannot coordinate private claims from residents or families against a nursing home because care is a contract between the resident and the nursing home.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: as the provision of care is a contract between the resident and the nursing home, MOH is unable to coordinate private claims from residents or their families against the nursing home

key_points.point: MOH supports nursing homes through manpower training grants and other support.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we do support our nursing homes through different support from manpower training grants to other support for nursing homes

key_points.point: On informing family members, MOH's first priority is to ensure improvements are done, lapses are rectified and residents' safety is not endangered.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: MOH's first priority is to make sure those improvements are done, lapses are rectified and to make sure nothing endangers the residents' safety

left_open: Whether there are plans to strengthen the regulatory regime for nursing homes.
The number of other nursing homes with significant lapses that are still being monitored.
Whether MOH will review foreign manpower requirements for smaller nursing home operators.
Whether audit findings will be shared with residents and families before regulatory action is confirmed.
supplementary: Monitoring of other nursing homes, support for smaller operators, and earlier sharing of audit findings with families.
